summary: Sustained telemetry-upload backpressure saturating local NVMe and causing GPU attach lag in dedicated slice
description: Issue summary: Customers on a dedicated slice owned by NovaHealth started seeing sustained p50/p95 throughput drops and GPU attach timeouts beginning 2026-03-12 14:10 UTC. Impact: production traffic experienced token generation slowdowns (p95 token latency increased from ~120ms to 950ms) and occasional attach failures (GPU attach timeouts causing 5xx fallbacks). High-level hypothesis: a telemetry/analytics sidecar from the customer is performing large, sustained uploads to local NVMe (logs/metrics checkpointing) which saturates NVMe IO queues on the nodes hosting their reserved slice. NVMe saturation is increasing kernel io_wait and interfering with the serving runtime's prefetch/paging and attach path, causing attach latency spikes that cascade into autoscaler misclassification and capacity churn.
impact: Customer-facing latency increase and dropped requests for NovaHealth enterprise clients during mid-day window. Estimated affected token throughput reduction ~30-55% on the customer's reserved GPUs during the window. Several downstream routes experienced automatic fallback to lower-capacity variants triggering budget/throughput issues.
environment_notes: Dedicated pool slice: slice_id=slice-cc9f, region: us-east-1, nodes are a heterogeneous mix (A100-40GB and A10G) pinned to customer's reserved pool. Sidecar version observed: nova-analytics-agent v2.4.1 (runs inside tenant sidecar namespace).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route NovaHealth traffic through dedicated slice slice-cc9f in prod-us-east-1.
2) Enable the nova-analytics-agent with bulk-checkpointing feature enabled (default config for customer's fleet).
3) Simulate sustained telemetry upload workload (approx 700-900MB/s write bursts to local NVMe across 6 pods for 8-12 minutes).
4) Observe NVMe write queue depth, kernel io_wait and gpu-attach latencies on affected nodes.
observed_logs: [2026-03-12T14:13:00Z] kubelet: high IO wait detected; throttling background prefetch threads

investigation_notes: 1) Correlated kernel nvme stats, kubelet io_wait and serving-runtime attach traces; timeline aligns with sidecar uploads starting at 14:10 UTC.
2) Nodes hosting slice-cc9f showed sustained nvme_utilization >95% and increased avg_submit_latency causing background prefetch threads to stall.
3) Serving runtime attach path relies on low-latency nvme metadata writes for checkpoint and KV cache operations; when writes block, attach() operation observed queueing and timeouts.
4) Autoscaler interpreted attach errors as capacity shortage and attempted to spin additional nodes, creating additional pressure as new nodes also accepted telemetry sidecars (tenant-level rollout).
5) No kernel OOMs or GPU driver crashes observed; issue is IO contention rather than GPU faults.
6) Similar but distinct from prior 'kv-cache growth' tickets; root cause here is sustained tenant-side NVMe bulk writes rather than prefetch growth.
immediate_mitigation: Applied blkio cgroup write-bandwidth limit (to ~200MB/s per affected sidecar) on the set of nodes hosting slice-cc9f. Reduced sidecar upload concurrency from 6 to 1. Temporarily increased autoscaler attach-error hysteresis to avoid reactive node churn.
long_term_fix: 1) Add tenant-side 'telemetry-throttle' annotation (engineering PR merged) and update default nova-analytics-agent to rate-limit bulk-checkpoint uploads during high-load windows. 2) Update Dedicated runbook to set node-level IO QOS for customer-side persistent sidecars. 3) Enhance serving-runtime to de-prioritize background writes (metadata/checkpoint) when io_wait crosses threshold. 4) Add observability alert for sustained nvme_utilization >85% on dedicated slices.
resolution_notes: Workaround reduced immediate impact: nvme util dropped from ~98% to ~60-70%, p95 token latency returned closer to baseline (210ms within 30 minutes of mitigation), attach error rate fell to baseline. Customer has scheduled config change and will deploy sidecar patch to disable bulk checkpointing during peak hours. Engineering PR created to add safer defaults and an annotation to opt in/out of high-volume uploads.

public_customer_message: We observed high-volume telemetry uploads from your analytics sidecar that saturated local disk IO on your dedicated nodes. We applied temporary upload throttles and autoscaler hysteresis to stabilize traffic. We recommend deploying the agent update (v2.4.2) which includes throttling defaults for dedicated slices and avoiding bulk-checkpointing during peak hours. Our team will follow up with a runbook and confirmation once the agent patch is live.
